status: Selected source-based interpretations; not independent ground truth or a complete legal history.

components.decision: The Court invalidated Connecticut’s prohibition on contraceptive use as applied to married couples.
components.scope: Legal use and marital privacy, not insurance coverage.
components.survey_fit: No suitably timed access question has been verified for this selection. Modern insurance questions cannot describe opinion in 1965.

components.decision: The Court invalidated unequal contraceptive-access rules for married and unmarried people.
components.scope: Equal protection in access, not a requirement that employers pay.
components.survey_fit: No verified earlier survey in this selection measures the married/unmarried distinction.

cases.name: Burwell v. Hobby Lobby Stores

components.decision: The Court held that applying the contraceptive mandate to the objecting closely held companies violated RFRA.
components.scope: This limited enforcement of the employer mandate; it did not prohibit contraceptive use or invalidate the entire coverage requirement.
components.locator: Alito majority opinion, Parts III–V, especially V.B.
components.survey_fit: Both polls address religious objections and employee coverage. They do not isolate closely held corporations, the four disputed methods, or alternative ways to provide coverage.

cases.interpretation_limit: The 5–4 judgment concerned statutory religious protections. The direction label describes the coverage mandate only, not a numerical balance between religious liberty and employee access.

components.decision: The Court vacated the judgments and remanded to allow consideration of an accommodation.
components.scope: The Court expressly did not decide the merits of the RFRA challenge.
components.locator: Per curiam opinion, paragraphs beginning “In light of the positions” and “The Court expresses no view”.
components.survey_fit: General preferences about coverage cannot turn this remand into approval or rejection of an exemption.
